correctness.rationale: Peter--Weyl decomposes L2_0 into every highest-weight m>=1 with eigenvalues U_m(c)/(m+1). The m=1,2 sectors force norm >=1/4, strictly for |c| !=1/4. At |c|=1/4 the m=3 sector is 7/32 and all m>=4 satisfy |lambda_m|<=4/(5 sqrt(15))<1/4; endpoints are norm-one. Center symmetry yields exactly two angles and the scalar self-adjoint spectrum yields the sharp kth powers. The code completed 3523 checks; it is supplemental, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual literature and research-record searches for the exact normalized-Chebyshev minimax, class-walk spectral contraction and alternative angle/trace formulas did not produce a covering claim. Two relevant primary full texts were read: one is a general compact-group spectral-gap framework, the other is a character estimate for centerless groups. A published SU(2) moment calculation does not imply this operator minimax from its stated claims; its full text was not read. The SO(3) quotient omits the fundamental SU(2) representation, so it does not cover this statement. Historical priority remains a risk, not a certified uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: The object is the natural single-conjugacy-class random-walk operator on SU(2), with an infinite family of Fourier irreducibles, not an arbitrary narrow coefficient table. The exact global minimax 1/4, both and only center-symmetric optimal classes, the precise two binding spin sectors, uniform high-spin exclusion and all-time operator-norm optimum together solve a meaningful constrained stability-design question. The SU(2) double cover adds a genuine fundamental-representation barrier absent on SO(3).
